tossups.text: The westernmost addition to this reserve is indented by the Barranca La Presa, which is dangerous due to its populations of feral dogs. The Cárcamo de Dolores terminates in this location. This non-Winter Palace location also boasts a famous Malachite Room and contains a clock tower known as the Tall Knight. A spiral-shaped history museum here is known as El Caracol, or the Snail. An emperor who once took up residence here constructed the Empress's Way leading to it; that street was later named Paseo de la Reforma. Another figure associated with it built the Tlaxpana Aqueduct to water a garden noted for its ahuehuete trees, one of which is 700 years old. This forest, whose name means "grasshopper hill," lies between the neighborhoods of Tacubaya (ta-ku-BA-ya) and Polanco in the borough of Miguel Hidalgo. For 10 points, name this second largest urban green space in Latin America containing the Baths of Netzahualcoyotl (net-za-wal-ko-YO-tl), the Xochipilli (so-chi-PI-yi) Fountain, as well as a namesake palace that was home to Mexico's presidents until 1939.

Composer and genre required. A movement from one of these works by this composer has a movement alternating between F-lydian and 3/8 D-major sections and is titled "Heiliger Dankgesang," and two of these works from the composer's "middle period" are titled "Harp" and "Serioso." Three of these works by this composer were commissioned by the Count Razumovsky, and the B-flat finale of one of these works was spun off into a separate work of this type known as the "Grosse Fuge." For 10 points, name these works for two violins, viola, and cello that were written by the composer of the "Moonlight Sonata."

Tom Wolfe's article "Radical Chic" describes a fundraising party hosted by Leonard Bernstein for members of this group. Full employment and exemption from military service were two of the Ten Points issued by this group. Howard Alk directed a documentary chronicling the murder of one member of this organization, Fred Hampton, who was killed by Chicago police in his apartment. The FBI's COINTELPRO sought to engineer feuds between this organization and the Blackstone Rangers. One founder of this group, which ran the Free Breakfast for Children program, was accused of murdering John Frey, an Oakland police officer. Founded by Bobby Seale and Huey Newton, for 10 points, name this militant African-American group active during the 1960s and 1970s.

A hearing about this incident had to be postponed after Henry Gonzalez wrote an angry letter to Jim Leach referring to him as "obstinate" and "obdurate." A flashpoint during this incident was created by a large banner reading "Go Home, Idiots!", put up by John Lauramoore. A court case stemming from this incident found that the Fifth Amendment prevents compelled production of incriminating documents that can't be described with reasonable particularity, upholding the refusal of Webster Hubbell to comply with a subpoena. This affair was first investigated by L. Jean Lewis, who fainted while she was being cross-examined. David Hale's testimony exposed the role of Jim and Susan McDougal in this event, which led Jim Guy Tucker to be removed from office. For 10 points, identify this scandal investigated by Ken Starr, which revealed some shady real estate investments made in Arkansas by Bill and Hillary Clinton.

In human physiology, this structure is essential for bronchi and bronchioles. It plays a key role in the respiratory system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this bronchus-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The bronchus is a key component of the Respiratory system, involved in bronchi and bronchioles.

tossups.text: The protagonist of this novel is assigned the position that demands the "capacity to see beyond" after being overlooked during the Ceremony of Twelve. That character, who is friends with Asher and Fiona, leaves the community with the infant Gabriel by sled after the realization of Gabriel's inevitable death. Only certain people can see color in, for ten points, what dystopian novel by Louis Lowry in which the title character teaches Jonas how to be the Receiver of Dreams?

In human physiology, this structure is essential for dermis components. It plays a key role in the integumentary system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this epidermis-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The epidermis is a key component of the Integumentary system, involved in dermis components.

tossups.text: Stuart Hall founded a center for the "studies" of this concept at the UK's University of Birmingham. This concept names a type of capital encompassing the taste of the upper class, as theorized by Pierre Bourdieu ("board-YUH"). This concept now consists of standardized goods that create a passive public through "mass deception" according to Adorno and Horkheimer's theory of this concept's "industry." This concept is called "personality writ large" in a book on its "Patterns" by Ruth Benedict, who contrasted America and Japan's "guilt" and "shame" forms of this concept. For 10 points, travelers may experience "shock" named for what concept that encompasses the beliefs and customs of a people?

One painting by this man depicts the lone dissenter, Jim Edgerton, interrupting a town meeting. This artist of Freedom of Speech painted a runaway boy seated on a barstool next to a police officer in a diner. In another of his paintings, The Problem We All Live With , a smashed and splattered tomato can be seen next to Ruby Bridges as she is escorted to school. This artist showed a woman serving turkey in Freedom from Want . For ten points, name this artist who painted The Four Freedoms and Rosie the Riveter .

In a sculpture by Etienne Maurice Falconet, Milo of Croton struggles with one of these animals while his hand is stuck in a tree trunk. Frédéric Bartholdi sculpted one of these animals in red sandstone to commemorate the Siege of Belfort, and St. Mark's Square in Venice contains a fifteen-foot bronze sculpture of a winged one of these animals atop a granite column. Four bronze sculptures of these animals lie at the base of Nelson's column. Chinese sculptures of these animals include them with either a ball or a cub and are used to guard imperial palaces and tombs from evil spirits. For 10 points, name these feline animals that make up the body of a sphinx.

This author describes "tak[ing] a knife/And cut[ting] the world in two," in his poem "Tired." At the end of another work by this poet, the speaker states "he slept like a rock or a man that's dead." This poet also described "ebony hands on each ivory key," and "droning a drowsy syncopated tune," in that work. This author of "The Weary Blues" also describes how his "soul has grown deep like" the title locations of his poem "The Negro Speaks of Rivers." For 10 points, name this American poet who describes "dry[ing] up like a raisin in the sun," in a poem that asks "What happens to a dream deferred?"

A model of this work was exhibited in the west alongside reconstructions of its creator's counter-reliefs and costumes from the Zanguezi show. T.M Shapiro was instrumental in the reconstruction of this building, as carried out by Pontus Hulten. Models of this building are held at the Moderna Museet and at the Centre Pompidou. Nikolai Punin argued that this building was an example of architecture that contained "Modern technical apparatuses promoting agitation and propaganda" and was "a place of the most intense movement." This building, called "the first Russian monument without a beard," was intended to cross a river, and a model for it was carried in a May Day Parade in St. Petersburg. Its interior was intended to hold four Comintern organizations in four glass containers and its exterior was a spiral of steel girders. For 10 points, name this never-built monument resembling steel scaffolding, designed by Vladimir Tatlin.
acceptableAnswers: The Monument to the Third International

tossups.text: This polity minted coins that depicted its rulers' heads encircled by two ears of wheat and used the motto "may this please the people." Features of this polity's architecture include protruding support beams called "monkey heads," as well as monuments decorated with false doors and windows. According to historians like Stuart Munro-Hay, this polity was the successor to the indigenous kingdom of Dʿmt ("DAH-muh-AHT"). The first person to receive an absentee funeral prayer in Mecca was a ruler of this polity whom Islamic sources refer to as Najashi; that ruler of this polity granted asylum to members of the ṣaḥāba during the First Hijra. Cosmas Indicopleustes recorded a bilingual inscription on a throne at this polity's chief port of Adulis that used the Greek, Sabaean, and Ge'ez ("ghee-IZ") scripts. For 10 points, kings such as Kaleb ("KAH-layb") and Ezana ("ee-ZAH-nah") promoted Christianity as the state religion of what ancient empire based in present-day Ethiopia?

This place was studied with the participant observation method of "soaking and poking" by a thinker who resolved a paradox about this place with the concept of "home style." A book titled for this place analyzes the "single-minded" behaviors of "credit claiming" and "position taking." A co-op set up by employees of this place is used as a parable of the "paradox of thrift" by Paul Krugman, since its members were reluctant to spend scrip worth half an hour of babysitting. Richard Fenno and David Mayhew studied this place, whose employees can use the "franking" privilege to send postage-free mail and may experience a "sophomore surge." For 10 points, name this American institution whose members may use pork-barrel spending to maintain an "incumbency advantage."
acceptableAnswers: prompt on the United States government

tossups.text: Okuninushi once slept in a room full of these creatures, which are typically depicted as white in Shinto mythology, and a princess who was to be sacrificed to one of these creatures was turned into a comb for safekeeping. Rainbow variants of these creatures are associated with the rain and the cycle of life in Aboriginal mythology. One of these creatures possessed a sword named "grass-cutter" in its fourth tail. Jormungandr is the Midgard type of these creatures, and a naga is one of these animals in Hindu mythology. For 10 points, name these animals which include vipers and pythons, a pair of which is featured on the caduceus.

Young's double-slit experiment showed a phase shift, proving that light functions as one of these phenomena. De Broglie stated that all matter has properties of both particles and these. These phenomena are classified into "longitudinal" and "transverse" by direction, and can be measured through their period, amplitude, and frequency. For 10 points, name these oscillations, such as sound, which transfer energy.

In this novel, the protagonist's mother idolized her father Doctor Foster to the point of sucking the fingers of his ether-bloated corpse. Another character in this novel was thought to be a witch due to her lack of a navel and carries around the bones of her father. In one episode from this novel, the protagonist meets Circe, an old ex-slave who leads him to his ancestral home of Shalimar, where he learns about his ancestors' supposed ability to fly. The protagonist of this novel is guided by his mother Pilate, rejects his father Macon, and has a showdown with his former friend Guitar. For 10 points, name this novel by Toni Morrison titled after a book of the Bible.

this structure is essential for sebaceous glands. It plays a key role in the integumentary system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this hair follicle-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The hair follicle is a key component of the Integumentary system, involved in sebaceous glands.

tossups.text: The main character of this novel recalls a time he pulled a switchblade out in class to dissect a worm and compares himself to Pip from Great Expectations. Cherry Valance and the main character of this novel often talk about how even though they have different lives, they both see the same sunset. This novel concludes by revealing that the entire story was written for an English paper so that the main character could get a C for the semester. In this novel, the last words of a character killed by a collapsing church allude to a Robert Frost poem; those words were "Stay Gold!" Johnny kills a Soc in self defense in, for 10 points, what S.E. Hinton novel that tells the story of the rivalry between the Socs and Greasers through the eyes of Ponyboy Curtis.

The only known chaperone protein for this structure is the trigger factor, and elongation factors promote binding to these organelles. In eukaryotes, the 3 prime terminus of its 18S portion attaches to the Kozak sequence, and the fMet initiator arrives at this organelle before it performs its most important function. This organelle has A, P, and E sites, and deacylated tRNA hangs out at the E-site before leaving this organelle. It is synthesized in the nucleolus and decodes mRNA in translation. For 10 points, name this organelle that is responsible for protein synthesis.

parts.text: The Caste War was so close to succeeding that its governor, isolated at the capital of Merida, offered sovereignty to the United States, Britain, and Spain if they were able to quell the revolt in this state. Chichen Itza can be found in its namesake land feature.
Governor Eduardo Bours Castelo probably wants you to visit this state's capital of Hermosillo, and it happens to be one of only two Mexican states to border Baja California.
This state's capital of Morelia is a UNESCO World Heritage site and the state is noted for its large monarch butterfly population.

bonuses.leadin: Identify the following about some Mexican states, for 10 points each.

parts.text: Name this photograph that shows several men and women in the lower-class portion of a steemer. Its use of a balcony and walkway to divide the picture into geometric shapes has been hailed as a proto-Cubist design.
The Steerage is a photograph by Alfred Stieglitz, who was married to this New Mexican painter. Many of her artworks depict relics of the desert, like cow skulls and vibrant flowers.
Stieglitz depicted several of these features in his Equivalents series. The development of panchromatic photographic emulsion allowed Stieglitz to photograph these features effectively.

bonuses.leadin: This photograph was first exhibited at its artist's Gallery 291. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this former CIA agent, who had her position leaked by Robert Novak after her husband, Joseph Wilson, investigated claims that Iraq had purchased uranium from Niger.

During the Plame Affair, Scooter Libby was convicted of lying to investigators. Libby is better known for working as the chief of staff for this then-vice president, who shot a guy in the face while quail hunting.
The Plame Affair occurred during the administration of this 43rd President, who authorized the invasion of Iraq and Afghanistan during the War on Terror in the first decade of the 2000s.
acceptableAnswers: ” accept any answers along the lines of Bush the son

bonuses.leadin: This person announced her candidacy for a house seat in New Mexico in May 2019. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this Inca system under which all able-bodied men from age 15 to 50 were mandated to work on government projects, often for more than 100 days per year.

Spain revived the mita system in this series of late 16th-century laws, which installed Inca regional leaders called kurakas as the head of repartimientos, or groups of natives from whom labor could be levied.
Perhaps most notoriously, the revived mit'a system provided labor for Potosí, where this metal was mined, refined using mercury in the patio process, and then exported.

bonuses.leadin: After Pizarro's conquests, this system was initially replaced with the encomienda system typical in the rest of the Spanish Americas. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with phagocytes and macrophages.
What is the main function of the phagocyte in the immune system?
Name another component of the immune system related to phagocytes and macrophages.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human immune system.

parts.text: Identify this "Belle of Amherst," the American poet of "I heard a fly buzz when I died" and "Because I could not stop for death."
This poet wrote about "The Village Blacksmith" and "Paul Revere's Ride," and composed the epic poem The Song of Hiawatha.
This poet wrote about one who "lies down to pleasant dreams" in a "meditation on death," Thanatopsis.

bonuses.leadin: Name some American poets, for 10 points each,

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with dermis components.
What is the main function of the epidermis in the integumentary system?
Name another component of the integumentary system related to dermis components.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human integumentary system.

parts.text: That experiment's lower-paid subjects felt a greater need to reduce this phenomenon, which arises from contradictions between one's beliefs and actions.

This psychologist conducted that experiment with James M. Carlsmith. With Henry Riecken and Stanley Schachter, this psychologist applied his theory of cognitive dissonance to a UFO cult in the work When Prophecy Fails.
After his work with Festinger, Schachter went on to develop a two-factor theory of these phenomena with Jerome E. Singer. Paul Ekman's universal types of these phenomena include sadness and anger.

bonuses.leadin: Subjects who were paid $1 to lie about a boring task rated it as more enjoyable than subjects paid $20 in one experiment. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this bespeckled Big Band leader who was known as the "King of Swing."
Goodman played this instrument. This single reed woodwind instrument looks like a straight black tube, and is a common lead instrument in Klezmer music.

A concert by Goodman's band at this location in 1938 is considered by music historians a major step towards jazz becoming "respectable" music. Located on 57th street in New York City, a joke says the way to get here is "practice."

bonuses.leadin: This artist and his big band popularized several jazz standards, such as "One O'Clock Jump" and "Swing Swing Swing." For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this early Renaissance artist, who sculpted a bronze David clad only in a hat and boots.
acceptableAnswers: Donato di Niccolò di Betto Bardi

parts.text: Donatello created this bronze equestrian statue of Erasmo da Narni, which stands in the Piazza del Santo in Padua.

Donatello used bronze to sculpt David and Gattamelata, but he used this medium to depict a haggard Penitent Magdalene, as well as John the Baptist. The ancient Palladium was also made of this material.

bonuses.leadin: This artist's sculpture Zuccone is thought to depict the prophet Habakkuk, although the nickname translates to "pumpkin-head." For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this short story collection that includes a story about a man who shoots himself in his hotel room after talking to the young girl Sybil on the beach.
The collection Nine Stories is written by this reclusive American author, who also penned Franny and Zooey and Catcher in the Rye.
This story from Nine Stories sees Seymour Glass say the title phrase to a girl on the beach before shooting himself in the head.

bonuses.leadin: Ginnie meets Franklin while waiting for Selena to gather the money to pay her share of the cab ride in this book's story "Just Before the War with the Eskimos." For 10 points each:

parts.text: This French composer challenged the idea that music should be listened to consciously with his idea of "furniture music" that would be listened to in the background. His more conventional music includes three Gymnopédies ("zhim-no-PAY-dees") for piano.

Music was defined as "organized sound" by this modernist composer, who used "sound-masses" in works like Ionisation. This French composer wrote Density 21.5 for Georges Barrère's ("ZHORZH bah-RAIR'S") platinum flute.

This composer stated "it is the gratuitous play of a child" as one of seven criteria for music in the book Formalized Music, which includes the FORTRAN code for his music program GENDY. His Pithoprakta is based on the Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution.

bonuses.leadin: Name these 20th-century composers who questioned the definition of music, for 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this leader of the Senones, the Gallic tribe that sacked Rome circa 390 BCE.

This man, who had been exiled to Ardea for supposedly stealing Etruscan gold from the treasury, supposedly emerged from his seclusion to drive Brennus and the Senones out of the Italian peninsula, though the story is disputed.
Camillus is also known for several victories over this group, whose leaders included the Roman traitor Coriolanus. They often allied themselves with the Aequi.

bonuses.leadin: This leader famously exclaimed "Vae victis!" after the conquered Romans pointed out that the scales he used to weigh his tribute were fixed. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name these linguistic constructions that "we live by" according to another book by George Lakoff.

Lakoff claims that the central metaphor of these people is the "strict father model" and writes in Moral Politics about what these people know and their opponents do not. Lakoff created the Rockridge Institute in an attempt to use linguistics against these people.

Lakoff's The Nature and Limits of Human Understanding discusses this theory, which states that many cognitive processes operate at a very low level and are inextricable from the basic biological pathways of sense-data.

bonuses.leadin: One book claims that these constructions were used to "justify the war in the Gulf" and that the entire conceptual system of political discourse is based on these things. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this great hall of the Einherjar, warriors who died heroically in battle.
These warrior maidens selected dead warriors to enter Valhalla. A notable one was Brynhildr.
Only half of the warriors enter Valhalla. The other half are sent to Fólkvangr, ruled over by this Vanir goddess of love, beauty, war, and death, who owns the necklace Brisingamen.

bonuses.leadin: This place hosts nightly feasts on Sæhrímnir the boar, who is resurrected each night. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this compound with formula "H 2 O"[H2O].

Groundwater is stored in these layers of permeable rock. Wells are dug into these structures to accessgroundwater, and a well is called "artesian" if this structure is under enough pressure to bring the water out of itwithout pumping.

Understanding the flow of fluids through permeable rock is important when considering the hazards of thispractice, in which high-pressure fluid is injected into shale in the hopes of extracting natural gas or oil.

bonuses.leadin: Darcy's Law explains how this substance can flow through a porous medium, as often happensunderground. For ten points each,

parts.text: Name this 1936 novel whose title is based on a passage from Paradise Lost.
In Dubious Battle was one of the earlier works of this author whose other works include The Red Pony, Travels with Charley, and East of Eden.
This Steinbeck work deals with a group of friends living near a sardine factory in Monterey, who try to throw a party for their friend Doc, who is modeled after Ed Ricketts.

bonuses.leadin: Jim Nolan and Doc Burton are Communist labor leaders, who help organize and provide for depression-era California fruit pickers in an ultimately unsuccessful strike. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with hemoglobin oxygen binding.
What is the main function of the diffusion in the respiratory system?
Name another component of the respiratory system related to hemoglobin oxygen binding.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human respiratory system.

parts.text: Name this author who concluded a trilogy with The Mirror and the Light. She won the 2012 Costa Book of the Year for Bring Up the Bodies.

Mantel's trilogy, which begins with Wolf Hall, follows the rise to power of a chief minister with this surname. A Lord Protector with this surname was the subject of Andrew Marvell's "An Horatian Ode."
Mantel won this award for the first two novels in the trilogy. The Man Group formerly sponsored this prize for English-language novels.

bonuses.leadin: A novel by this author includes fictional versions of Lord Chancellor Stephen Gardiner and Jane Seymour. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this process where a single species evolves into several different species due to the occupation of distinct ecological niches.

These organisms, a group of fifteen specific species, famously evolved from a single species through adaptive radiation. Due to the particular environmental conditions present on the different island that they inhabited, they developed differently shaped beaks.

Organisms can also undergo this type of speciation, which occurs when they are unable to mate with each other. Causative agents of this type of speciation include polyploidy and incompatible mating structures.

bonuses.leadin: Explanations for why this type of speciation occurred so rapidly in the Cambrian explosion include increased oxygen levels in the atmosphere. For 10 points each:
